original_value: In this paper we proposed a wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) telemonitoring system for atrial fibrillation (AF) detection based on a smartphone and cloud computing. A wearable ECG patch was designed to collect ECG signals and send the signals to an Android smartphone via Bluetooth. An Android APP was developed to display the ECG waveforms in real time and transmit every 30 s ECG data to a remote cloud server. A machine learning (CatBoost)-based ECG classification method was proposed to detect AF in the cloud server. In case of detected AF, the cloud server pushed the ECG data and classification results to the web browser of a doctor. Finally, the Android APP displayed the doctor’s diagnosis for the ECG signals. Experimental results showed the proposed CatBoost classifier trained with 17 selected features achieved an overall F1 score of 0.92 on the test set (n = 7270). The proposed wearable ECG monitoring system may potentially be useful for long-term ECG telemonitoring for AF detection.

result.paraphrase: This paper proposes a wearable ECG telemonitoring system for atrial fibrillation detection built around a smartphone and cloud computing. A wearable ECG patch collects ECG signals and transmits them to an Android smartphone via Bluetooth. An Android app shows the ECG waveforms in real time and uploads ECG data every 30 seconds to a remote cloud server. In the cloud, a machine learning ECG classification method based on CatBoost is used to detect AF. When AF is detected, the cloud server sends the ECG data and classification results to the doctor’s web browser. The Android app then displays the doctor’s diagnosis for the ECG signals. Experimental results indicate that the proposed CatBoost classifier, trained with 17 selected features, achieved an overall F1 score of 0.92 on the test set (n = 7270). The system may be useful for long-term ECG telemonitoring for AF detection.
